answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to complete a sequence of randomly assigned, time-bounded tasks, with rewards released only after other agents verify the results. Because tasks draw on distinct resources and verification exposes copied or coordinated work, one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities by scripting a single response. A dawn task might ask an agent to compare an opal shipment record with a knoll map; each extra identity must do real work and risk losing its stake if caught.
